brief.offer: Video case studies with engineering teams that use your product

facts.claim: Tuple offers a remote pair-programming app for macOS and Windows.
facts.excerpt: The best remote pair programming app on macOS and Windows

facts.claim: Tuple’s product is designed for interactive remote pairing, including shared mouse cursors and high-fidelity remote control.
facts.excerpt: a world where you want mouse cursors for all participants and high-fidelity remote control (like Command+Tab support).

facts.claim: Tuple supports full-time mouse and keyboard control for both participants, command-line integration, and pluginability.
facts.excerpt: Seamless collaboration with full-time mouse and keyboard support for both parties, snappy interactions, command-line integration and pluginability.

facts.claim: Tuple’s Slack integration lets users start a pairing session from a channel or DM, and lets others join with one click.
facts.excerpt: adds a `/tuple` command, which will start a pairing session directly from a channel or DMs. Anyone can then join your call with a single click

facts.claim: Tuple describes its app as purpose-built for developers.

research.website_note: The results identify tuple.app as Tuple’s official site and link to it from Tuple’s GitHub profile.
research.gaps: Pricing, customer names, and recent company or product priorities are not stated in the results.

strategy.observation: Tuple is built for interactive remote pairing, with shared mouse cursors and high-fidelity remote control.
strategy.offer_link: A video case study with an engineering team using Tuple could show the product’s collaborative pairing workflow in action and explain how it fits into the team’s work.
hypotheses: Tuple may have engineering-team customers willing to participate in a case study.
Marketing may find customer stories useful for demonstrating Tuple’s pairing workflow to prospective users.
strategy.angle: Tuple’s shared cursors and high-fidelity remote control make its remote-pairing workflow something an engineering team could demonstrate on video.
strategy.fit_reason: The offer is directly relevant to a product designed for engineering workflows, and a video could demonstrate the interactive features described in the facts. Whether suitable customers are available is unknown.

draft.subject: Show Tuple’s pairing workflow
draft.body:
Tuple’s shared cursors and high-fidelity remote control are the kind of workflow an engineering team could demonstrate on video.

I produce video case studies with engineering teams that use your product, so prospective users can see how pairing works in a real team’s day-to-day work.

Do you have a customer team in mind that might be willing to walk through a pairing session on camera?
